To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) modules based on syntactical locality are the most effective, (2) modules based on semantic localization are more effective than those based on MEX modules, and (3) modules based on MEX locality are not effective at all.

1) the three module extraction approaches are not equally good in terms of the quality of the extracted modules; and 2) the syntactic locality approach is the best choice, because it is the only one that is applicable to large-scale ontologies.

(1) MEX modules are the most expressive and the least expensive modules; (2) modules based on semantic and syntactic locality are the least expressive and the most expensive modules; and (3) modules based on syntacitc locality are the most expensive modules, but they are still cheap.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how much of the ontology has to be considered in order to be able to reason about a given concept or a given set of concepts.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in terms of module size, syntactic locality is the best choice for ontologies in general, whereas for ontologies that are not too expressive (in particular, for OWL DL ontolo- gies) semantic locality is the best option.
syntactic locality is a good approximation of semantic locality, which in turn is a good approximation to MEX modules, and thus a good approximation to the relevant axioms in an ontology.

the three notions of locality-based modules, which are all sound, are all useful, and that the syntactic locality modules are the best choice, as they are cheap to compute, but still give a good approximation of the relevant part of the ontology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in practice, syntactic locality modules can be used in place of semantic locality modules, and semantic locality modules can be safely used in place of MEX modules.
, in general, syntactic locality is not a good approximation of semantic locality, and semantic locality is not a very good approximation of MEX modules.
syntactic locality-based modules are a good choice for ontology reuse and integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
syntactic locality modules are a very poor approximation of semantic locality modules, and that MEX modules are a very good approximation of semantic locality, and thus semantic locality, modules.
syntactic modules are not only cheaper to extract, but they also perform well compared to semantic modules.

, for a wide class of ontologies, syntactic modules are a cheap and cheerful approximation of semantic modules, which are in turn a cheap and cheerful (approximation of an) approximation of MEX modules.
